whatWasTriedAndFoundSound: Case of the issue key. The batch keys its five companion statements on r.PathValue("key") where the sequential path keyed them on the issue.Key the row answered. That is safe only because issues.key is `text primary key` (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0001_init.up.sql:10), an exact match, so the two strings cannot differ; a case-insensitive key column would have made every batched read of a differently-cased key answer an issue with no artifacts, asks or children.

Version order. artifactVersionsStatement orders `by v.artifact_id, v.number` where the per-artifact loadVersions ordered `by v.number` (5dc21cb9:packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/artifacts.go:1377), and the artifact id both sides key on is `id::text` against `v.artifact_id::text`, so the grouping and the per-artifact order are preserved. Proved by TestProbeVersionGroupingMatchesPerArtifactLoader and by the suite catching the reversed-order mutation.

Mark order in StripAnchorMarks. writtenTree filters marks through renderedMarks, which keeps their order, not through visibleMarks, which sorts them and then reorders them by renderMarkRank; had it used visibleMarks, the stripped tree's marks would have come out in rendering order rather than canonical order, which no render shows and every caller that keeps the tree would see. It does not, and the 16,135-line tree comparison confirms it.

The pool. store.Pool.SendBatch carries the same guard as Query (pool.go:526, refusing ErrNestedAcquire to a caller already holding a connection) and getIssue is reached from no connection-holder; no batch callback acquires anything, and both batches' results are closed before readRouteRoster's HTTP read. The 420-refused-read storm shows the error path returns its connection.

Empty-list parity. scanExternalLinks, collectArtifacts, scanIssueChildren and issueOpenAsksOf each return a non-nil empty slice, so an issue with none still answers [] and not null - checked on the four stripped shapes as well as the full fixture.
